gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the original Anker SOLIX F3800's solar input depends on its firmware: on firmware 1.7.8 or earlier it takes only 10 A at 11–32 V (25 A at 32–60 V), and 2.1.1 or later allows 27 A from 15–60 V. Below 32 V, an un-updated unit is therefore limited to about 320 W per port instead of 1,200 W.
standout_why: Pages compared: the cited Anker page (ankersolix.com/products/f3800, which now loads F3800 Plus content), the cited EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 product pages, the uncited Solar Waypoint three-way comparison and WattNerds. Solar Waypoint and the Anker F3800 page give the F3800 only as '11–60 V, 27 A, 1,200 W per port' or as a 2,400 W total. None of the pages I opened gives the firmware-dependent current limits. They also name no expansion-battery models and give no guidance on wiring panels together. The Anker page ChatGPT cited does carry the F3800-vs-Plus voltage comparison, and probably the FAQ saying rooftop solar can't recharge the unit through the Home Power Panel, so those two points are not new.
decides: This doesn't change the pick. It adds a condition to answering 'does solar help' for anyone buying a base F3800 (often discounted, refurbished or second-hand): update to firmware 2.1.1 or later before relying on low-voltage panels. Otherwise a parallel bank of 12 V-class panels (under 32 V) is limited to 10 A, about 320 W per port. That is still enough to cover a 0.6–1 kWh/day freezer on a sunny day, but far below the 400–800 W ChatGPT assumed. The F3800 Plus avoids this with 11–165 V, 17 A inputs. For homes with rooftop solar, Anker says the F3800 Plus can't be recharged from rooftop solar through the Home Power Panel during an outage. Portable panels must plug into the unit directly, which supports ChatGPT's 'battery + portable panels' advice for that setup.

findings.label: Solar input limits by firmware
findings.value: Firmware 1.7.8 or earlier: 11–32 V at 10 A, 32–60 V at 25 A, 1,200 W max per port. Firmware 2.1.1 or later: 11–15 V at 10 A, 15–60 V at 27 A, 1,200 W max per port. Two XT-60 ports, 2,400 W total.
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus + Expansion Battery | Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: Comparison spec on the maker's page. My arithmetic: on old firmware, an array under 32 V is capped at 10 A × ≤32 V = ≤320 W per port (≈200 W at a 20 V operating point), against 1,200 W after the update.

findings.label: Solar input per port, and stated damage limit
findings.value: 2 ports, 11–165 V, 17 A max, 1,600 W max each (3,200 W total). Anker: 'Exceeding 165V may cause damage to the solar input ports.'
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus + Expansion Battery | Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: Same figures appear on ankersolix.com/products/f3800, which now shows F3800 Plus content.

findings.label: Rooftop solar during an outage (maker's exclusion)
findings.value: Can't be recharged from rooftop solar through the Home Power Panel during an outage; solar panels must connect directly to the unit's 11–165 V inputs
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus + Expansion Battery | Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: From the FAQ on the maker's page. The page ChatGPT cited (ankersolix.com/products/f3800) appears to carry the same FAQ.

findings.label: Expansion battery and maximum count
findings.value: BP3800, 3,840 Wh, 72.8 lb; up to 6 per F3800 Plus
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus + Expansion Battery | Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: Page wording: 'Up to 6 × Expansion Batteries (3.84kWh each)'. My arithmetic: one BP3800 brings a single unit to 7,680 Wh.

findings.label: Other stated limits
findings.value: 240 V output can't be used while charging from 120 V AC. 'Designed for North American Power Standards Only.' Generator Adapter supports a single F3800 Plus only. With a 120 V generator, the TT-30R outlet works on L1 only.
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus + Expansion Battery | Anker SOLIX US

findings.label: Switchover time
findings.value: 20 ms when plugged into a 120 V wall outlet; 30 ms F3800 Plus to generator; 50 ms generator to F3800 Plus
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3800 Portable Power Station - 3840Wh | 6000W - Anker SOLIX US
